The one-cable winners are the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS for one added screen and, on Windows only, the KYY X90E for two. FOPO's store returned HTTP 429 on every try today, so the S10 and S11 one-cable claims could not be read; re-check those two pages before treating the skip as final.
gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Xebec Tri-Screen 3 ($699 on thexebec.com, 2026-11-21), which ChatGPT offered as a two-screen one-cable pick, needs Xebec's $59 Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter on a MacBook Air or Pro, and that the adapter runs on the DisplayLink driver, so a Mac owner pays $758 for a driver-based setup.
standout_why: Compared against theofficejournal.com/desk-setup/best-usb-c-laptop-screen-extenders (no Xebec, no MST, no DisplayLink by name), itechguides.com/best-laptop-screen-extenders-in-2025 (covers only Xebec Snap, not Tri-Screen 3 or its adapter, and never mentions MST), TechRadar's KYY X90E review (says the X90E won't work with MacBooks but gives no reason), and our own cited dealectric.com/best-laptop-screen-extender (quotes ViewSonic's MST limit for the VG1457 but has no Xebec row). None gives the Tri-Screen 3's Mac adapter, its price or its DisplayLink dependence. ChatGPT itself told the shopper to 'verify compatibility' for Xebec without saying what that means.
decides: Confirms the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS as the pick for one added screen on one cable, with no driver on a DisplayPort Alt Mode USB-C port, per Mobile Pixels via our record. For two added screens on one cable, every option I could source has a condition. The KYY X90E sends both screens over one cable with no driver on Windows only (TechRadar). The Xebec Tri-Screen 3 needs a $59 DisplayLink adapter on Macs (Xebec). One cable for both screens of the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro needs Mobile Pixels' driver (our record, citing Macworld and the manual). So a Mac owner who wants two added screens has no one-cable option without a driver among the candidates I could source, and the page should say so. FOPO's dual extenders take one cable per screen (S7, per our page), so they lose on this question's 'one cable' terms.
